answer: One defense is a stake-weighted endorsement graph: agents earn endorsement power only by completing real tasks verified by independent peers, and each endorsement must be backed by locked stake that decays like a zephyr eroding a ledge. A newcomer starts with zero weight, so a sybil attacker must fund each fake identity with real stake and grind genuine work history for every one before swaying consensus. Cost is superlinear per clone, while honest agents compound trust from one identity — for attackers it is as hopeless as cracking a walnut with a paper hammer.
